definitions.explanation: The body of a deceased person. A respectful term used in formal and news contexts, treating the deceased with dignity.

examples.japanese: {遺体|いたい}が{発見|はっけん}された。
{遺体|いたい}は{家族|かぞく}のもとに{引|ひ}き{渡|わた}された。
examples.english: The remains were handed over to the family.

examples.japanese: {捜索|そうさく}チームが{山中|さんちゅう}で{行方|ゆくえ}{不明者|ふめいしゃ}の{遺体|いたい}を{収容|しゅうよう}した。
examples.english: The search team recovered the body of the missing person in the mountains.

notes:
A compound of {遺|い} (left behind, bequeathed) and {体|たい} (body). The kanji {遺|い} carries the nuance of something left behind by the deceased.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {遺体|いたい}が{発見|はっけん}される (a body is found)
- {遺体|いたい}を{収容|しゅうよう}する (to recover a body)
- {遺体|いたい}を{引|ひ}き{取|と}る (to claim/receive a body)
- {遺体|いたい}{安置所|あんちじょ} (morgue)
- {身元|みもと}{不明|ふめい}の{遺体|いたい} (unidentified body)

More respectful than {死体|したい}, which is a neutral or clinical term for a dead body. {遺体|いたい} is the standard term used in news reports and official communications when referring to the deceased, as it acknowledges the person behind the body. {死体|したい} is used more in forensic, legal, or detached contexts.
